subject: physics
title: Gas pressure, volume and doing work on a gas
key_idea: (Separate science) A gas can be compressed or expanded by pressure changes. At constant temperature, **pressure × volume = constant**. Doing work on a gas, such as pumping a bicycle tyre, increases its internal energy and its temperature.

sections.heading: Pressure on surfaces and compressing gases

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers the direction of the force from a gas and what happens when a gas is compressed or expanded.

items: A gas can be compressed or expanded by changing the pressure on it.
The pressure of a gas produces a net force at right angles to the wall of its container.
This is true for any surface in contact with the gas.
The force comes from the particles colliding with the surface.
Gases can be compressed or expanded by pressure changes.
The force from gas pressure acts at right angles to any surface.

sections.heading: Pressure and volume at constant temperature

blocks.text: (Separate science) Here the mass of gas and its temperature stay the same. Only the volume changes.

items: If the volume decreases, the particles are closer together.
They hit the walls more often, so the frequency of collisions increases.
The speed of the particles does not change, because the temperature is constant.
A larger total force on a smaller area means a greater pressure.
If the volume increases, the particles hit the walls less often and the pressure decreases.

p × V is constant, so halving the volume doubles the pressure.

blocks.text: (Separate science, Higher tier for AQA) Compressing a gas quickly transfers energy to it and can raise its temperature.

items.meaning: The transfer of energy by a force.

items: Pushing the piston of a bicycle pump applies a force to the air.
Work is done on the air, so energy is transferred to it.
The internal energy of the gas increases.
The average kinetic energy of the particles increases, so the temperature of the gas increases.
The pump gets warm.
Doing work on a gas increases its internal energy.
The kinetic energy of the particles increases, so the temperature rises.
A bicycle pump gets warm because work is done on the air.

checks.q: A fixed mass of gas at constant temperature is compressed. Explain why its pressure increases.
checks.a: The particles are closer together, so they collide with the walls more frequently. There is a larger total force on the same area, so the pressure increases.

checks.q: A gas at 200 000 Pa has a volume of 0.050 m³. It is compressed to 0.020 m³ at constant temperature. Calculate the new pressure.
Explain why the air in a bicycle pump gets warm when the pump is used.
checks.a: Work is done on the air. This increases the kinetic energy of the air particles, so the temperature increases.

mistakes.wrong: When the plunger is pushed in, the particles move faster so they collide more often.
mistakes.right: The temperature is constant, so the kinetic energy does not change. The collision mark is not credited if linked to an increase in kinetic energy. Say the particles are closer together.

mistakes.wrong: When the volume is halved, the pressure is halved.
mistakes.right: Pressure × volume is constant. When the volume is halved the pressure doubles.

mistakes.wrong: Pumping more air into a tyre raises the pressure because the air particles move faster.
mistakes.right: The temperature and volume do not change. There are more particles, so more collisions with the walls per second. Do not link it to temperature or speed.

worked_example.question: The pressure of the helium in a balloon is 100 000 Pa. The volume of the balloon is 0.030 m³. The balloon is compressed at a constant temperature causing the volume to decrease to 0.025 m³. No helium leaves the balloon. Calculate the new pressure in the balloon.
worked_example.tip: One mark for each step. Substituting into p₁V₁ = p₂V₂ earns the first two marks.

exam_phrases: P₁ × V₁ = P₂ × V₂
particles in (rapid) (random) motion collide with the walls of the container
when the volume decreases the rate / frequency of collisions increases
force on the walls increases so pressure increases
pressure = force / area
work is done (in compressing the air)
increases the kinetic energy of the (air) particles

mistakes.wrong: The particles collide more, so the pressure rises.
mistakes.right: This is a limited answer. Also say the particles are in random motion and collide with the walls, exerting a force. When the volume decreases the rate of collisions increases, so the force on the walls and the pressure increase.

mistakes.wrong: The air in the bicycle pump gets warm because of friction.
mistakes.right: Ignore friction. Work is done in compressing the air, which increases the kinetic energy of the air particles.

mistakes.wrong: Using 4.8 litres as 4800 in a pressure and volume calculation.
mistakes.right: A power-of-ten error loses marks. Keep the same unit for V₁ and V₂.

worked_example.question: When a bicycle pump is used to inflate a bicycle tube, the air in the bicycle pump gets warm. You should ignore any effects of friction in the pump. Explain why the air in the bicycle pump gets warm.
answer_points: Work is done in compressing the air.
This increases the kinetic energy of the air particles (the thermal energy of the system).
worked_example.tip: One mark for work being done and one mark for the increase in kinetic energy. Ignore friction.

work is being done on the gas

mistakes.wrong: The particles are less likely to hit the sides of the container.
mistakes.right: Less likely is ignored. Say there are fewer collisions, or less frequent collisions, with the sides.

mistakes.wrong: A bicycle pump gets warmer because heat comes from the tyre.
mistakes.right: Heat transfer from the tyre is ignored. Say work is being done on the gas, so the speed and kinetic energy of the particles increase.

mistakes.wrong: If the volume of a gas is halved, the number of collisions per second is halved.
mistakes.right: The number of collisions per second is doubled, and so is the pressure.

worked_example.question: A gas is enclosed in a container with a piston. The teacher slowly moves the piston outwards until the gas has twice its original volume. The temperature of the gas is kept constant. Explain how and why the pressure in the container changes.
answer_points: The rate of collisions with the sides of the container decreases, so there are fewer collisions.
The collisions are less frequent, with more time between them.
worked_example.tip: Do not write the reverse argument or use the words less likely.
